thread:
maria: quick heads-up — i'm prototyping a change to the /rerank output. thinking we should support two score shapes: compact (single float per candidate) and verbose (normalized_score + explain_tokens + provenance). want opinions before we land an API minor.
ken: curious — what's the motivation for verbose? more telemetry for debugging? :thinking_face:
maria: yep two things: (1) easier QA for model regressions (we can tie back to tokens that drove the decision), (2) console can show a simple explanation panel for customers without parsing logs.
ash: +1 on the UX side but worried about payload size. some customers send 500 candidates; verbose will explode tokens and affect latency/billing.
jules: can we decouple billing? e.g., charge for candidate scoring units but not for optional explain payload unless requested? that buys us flexibility.
samir: important: also consider model selection. if we add provenance we should include a small model_hint field indicating which model variant scored that candidate (affinity + fallback). otherwise provenance is ambiguous in multi-model fans.
ken: proposal: keep default shape compact: {score: float}. Add `score_mode` query param that can be `compact|verbose`. verbose adds `{normalized_score, explain_tokens, model_hint}`. default stays compact so no perf/regression.
maria: that sounds okay, but we need to gate verbose by tenant-level quota. otherwise cheap tenants can request verbose on every call and blow our egress/compute.
ash: how about automatic sampling? verbose on 1% of requests for most tenants, full verbose only if tenant toggles a console flag or uses an explicit header `X-RERANK-EXPLAIN: 1`.
jules: and enforce soft-cap per-tenant: `max_verbose_per_minute`. console should surface usage and a link to toggle sampling -> gives customers control and reduces surprise invoice spikes.
samir: one more: fallback model routing. if primary model not available and we fallback to smaller model, normalized_score semantics should indicate whether scores are comparable across models. otherwise customers will misinterpret.
maria: good point. maybe add `score_calibration: "model-aware" | "naive"`. model-aware means we include a calibration_tag so console can annotate confidence differences.
ken: minor nit: keep compact size minimal — use `s` for score in compact format to save bytes? e.g., `[{id: 'c1', s: 0.87}]` vs verbose `[{id, normalized_score, explain_tokens}]`.
ash: i hate single-letter keys for maintainability but we do operate at scale. maybe only use short keys internally and console maps to friendly names.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary plan reminder — any schema change needs a 2-week canary rollout with sampling flagged and a migration shim for old clients. start with header `X-RERANK-SCHEMA: v2-preview`.
maria: thanks. action items i hear: (1) implement `score_mode` param with default compact, (2) add `X-RERANK-EXPLAIN` header to opt-in, (3) tenant-level soft caps + sampling, (4) add `model_hint` and `score_calibration` fields for verbose, (5) console telemetry + toggle UX, (6) canary header + migration shim.
jules: i'll draft the console UX for the toggle + quota graphs.
samir: i'll write a short spec for model_hint semantics and calibration tags.
ken: i'll prototype compact vs verbose serializers — i'll test payload size tradeoffs with 50/200/500 candidates.
maria: cool. if no blockers i'll open the API PR and include a backwards-compatible shim. pinging @here for visibility.
ash: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: created canary issue #RERANK-823 in the release board.
